terms.meaning: India's Union Legislature: the President plus the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
The lower house, directly elected by citizens above 18.
The upper house, mostly elected by state assemblies, not by citizens.
The Lok Sabha member chosen by the others to run the house and keep order.
The Prime Minister and ministers form the Union Cabinet; each minister answers for a department.
A vote by which a Lok Sabha majority can remove the Cabinet.

items.name: India's union
items.example: The Union Government is also called the Central Government.

items.name: Lok Sabha facts
items.formula: Up to 552 seats, five-year term; a member must be at least 25.
items.example: A member can contest any number of times.

items.name: Who can't be a Lok Sabha member
items.formula: A non-citizen, someone holding a government post, the mentally unfit, the imprisoned, or an insolvent.
items.example: Insolvent means unable to pay one's debts.

items.name: Rajya Sabha facts
items.formula: Up to 250 seats: 238 elected by state assemblies and 12 nominated by the President.
items.example: Members must be 30, serve six years; the Vice-President is Chairman.

items.name: Powers of Parliament
items.formula: Makes laws, controls money (the Financial Bill starts in the Lok Sabha), questions ministers, amends the Constitution.
items.example: No tax or spending without Parliament's approval.

items.name: MPs and the opposition
items.formula: MPs have freedom of speech in Parliament that no court can question.
items.example: The opposition leader points out the government's lapses.

items.name: The President
items.formula: Head of the Republic and first citizen; lives in Rashtrapati Bhavan; elected by MPs and state MLAs.
items.example: Must be at least 35; term five years.

items.name: Powers of the President
items.formula: Appoints the PM and ministers, signs bills into Acts, commands the forces, appoints judges, grants pardons.
items.example: No bill becomes an Act without the President's assent.

items.name: The Vice-President
items.formula: Elected by both houses; at least 35; term five years.
items.example: Chairs the Rajya Sabha and acts for the President when absent.

items.name: Role of the Prime Minister
items.formula: Head of government and leader of the Lok Sabha; allots and reshuffles portfolios.
items.example: When the PM resigns, the whole Cabinet goes.

items.name: Parliament buildings
items.formula: Rashtrapati Bhavan has 340 rooms, finished in 1929.
items.example: The new Parliament House (28-05-2023) has an 888-seat Lok Sabha hall and a 384-seat Rajya Sabha hall.

mistakes.text: Ages: Lok Sabha 25, Rajya Sabha 30, President and Vice-President 35.
The Rajya Sabha is chaired by the Vice-President; the Lok Sabha has a Speaker elected by its members.
Lok Sabha members serve five years; Rajya Sabha members serve six.
